stemMd: A membrane allows water but not sucrose to cross. Side X contains 0.1 mol/L sucrose and side Y contains 0.4 mol/L sucrose, initially at equal pressure. Which net movement begins?

options.label: B
options.textMd: Equal net flows of water in both directions

options.label: E
options.textMd: No water movement because sucrose cannot cross

explanationMd: The more concentrated sucrose solution has lower water potential at equal pressure. Water therefore moves from the dilute side X to the concentrated side Y until opposing pressure or concentration changes reduce net flux.

distractorRationale.b: Equal opposing flows would give zero net flow, unlike the stated initial conditions.
distractorRationale.d: The membrane is impermeable to sucrose.
distractorRationale.e: Solute impermeability is what sustains the osmotic difference.
distractorRationale.c: This reverses the initial osmotic direction.
